own_solution.law: Einstein's photoelectric equation gives Kmax = hc/lambda - phi. Converting mc² to 511000 eV, v = 300000 sqrt(2Kmax/511000) km/s. At 250 nm, Kmax = 2.66 eV and v = 967.981 km/s. Shortenings of 35, 55 and 80 nm give wavelengths 215, 195 and 170 nm and speeds 1105.17, 1195.73 and 1326.34 km/s, respectively.
assumptions: The stated single-photon photoelectric model applies.
The fastest emitted electrons lose energy only through the work function.
The non-relativistic kinetic-energy relation applies, as explicitly requested.
The measured electrons in T860D are emitted after the source is tuned.
The second lamp illuminates the screen independently of the metal illumination.

defect_reasons.rendering_not_minimal: TA8F1 and TCF8E omit the 55 nm value carried by the other wavelength-shift sentences, violating the review instructions' numerical-matching requirement even though the packet explicitly identifies these omissions as intentional numeral-free controls.

counterexamples: An earlier wavelength of 249 nm satisfies TA8F1's 'slightly shorter' wording but does not represent the 55 nm shortening stated in TF3E8.
Shortening the second lamp's wavelength by 1 nm satisfies TCF8E's 'a small amount' wording but does not represent TEF5E's 55 nm shortening.
